mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.A: A convex lens diverges parallel rays; a concave lens converges them.
options.B: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus; a concave lens diverges them as if originating from a virtual focus.
options.C: Both convex and concave lenses converge parallel rays to the same point.
options.D: Both convex and concave lenses diverge parallel rays.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus; a concave lens diverges them as if originating from a virtual focus.
mcqs.explanation: A convex (converging) lens brings parallel incident rays to a real focal point on the opposite side of the lens. A concave (diverging) lens spreads parallel rays so that they appear to originate from a virtual focal point on the same side as the object. Options A, C and D describe the opposite behavior, making B the only correct description.

mcqs.question: A thin lens is placed on a sheet of graph paper. A ray drawn to pass through the lens without any change in direction indicates which point of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre of a thin lens is the point through which any incident ray passes undeviated. This property is used to locate the centre experimentally. The principal focus and focal point are related to where refracted rays converge or appear to diverge, not where they pass straight through.

mcqs.question: A student claims that the principal focus of a concave lens lies on the same side as the object. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The claim is correct; the principal focus is on the object's side.
options.B: The claim is incorrect; the principal focus of a concave lens is on the opposite side of the lens from the object.
options.C: The claim is incorrect; the principal focus of a concave lens is virtual and lies on the same side as the object.
options.D: The claim is correct; both convex and concave lenses have principal focus on the object's side.

mcqs.answer: The claim is incorrect; the principal focus of a concave lens is virtual and lies on the same side as the object.
mcqs.explanation: For a concave (diverging) lens, the principal focus is virtual; it is located on the same side of the lens as the object because the refracted rays appear to diverge from that point. Option C states this correctly. Option A incorrectly says the claim is correct without mentioning the virtual nature. Option B places the focus on the opposite side, which is true for a convex lens only. Option D is wrong for convex lenses.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms an image of a distant object at a distance of 20 cm from the lens on the opposite side. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: When the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the focal point of a convex lens. Hence the distance of the image from the lens equals the focal length. The image is 20 cm away, so the focal length is 20 cm. The other options are unrelated values.

mcqs.question: Which ray diagram correctly shows the image formed by a convex lens when the object is placed beyond twice the focal length (beyond 2F)?

options.A: Object beyond 2F; a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the focus, a ray through the centre passes undeviated, producing a real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F.
options.B: Object beyond 2F; all rays diverge after the lens, producing an upright, virtual image beyond 2F.
options.C: Object beyond 2F; parallel rays diverge as if coming from a virtual focus, giving a virtual, upright image on the same side as the object.
options.D: Object beyond 2F; a ray through the focus emerges parallel, and a ray through the centre forms a real, enlarged image beyond 2F.

mcqs.answer: Object beyond 2F; a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the focus, a ray through the centre passes undeviated, producing a real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens with the object beyond 2F, the standard ray diagram uses (i) a ray parallel to the principal axis that passes through the focal point after refraction, (ii) a ray through the centre that goes straight, and (iii) a ray through the focus that emerges parallel. These rays intersect between F and 2F, giving a real, inverted, reduced image. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect ray behaviours or image characteristics.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms a real image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. The image is:

options.A: Real, inverted, and formed at 15 cm on the opposite side of the lens.
options.B: Real, inverted, and formed at 15 cm on the same side as the object.
options.C: Virtual, upright, and formed at 15 cm on the same side as the object.
options.D: Virtual, upright, and formed at 15 cm on the opposite side of the lens.

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, and formed at 15 cm on the opposite side of the lens.
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (sign convention: u = +30 cm, f = +10 cm), we get 1/v = 1/10 – 1/30 = 2/30 = 1/15, so v = +15 cm. Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side of the lens, and real images formed by convex lenses are inverted. Hence option A is correct; the other options misplace the image or describe it as virtual/upright.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a convex lens compared to a concave lens?

options.A: Convex lens diverges light; concave lens converges light.
options.B: Convex lens converges parallel light to a real focus; concave lens diverges light as if originating from a virtual focus.
options.C: Both lenses have the same effect on parallel light.
options.D: Convex lens has no focal point, while concave lens does.

mcqs.answer: Convex lens converges parallel light to a real focus; concave lens diverges light as if originating from a virtual focus.
mcqs.explanation: A convex (converging) lens brings parallel incident rays to a real focal point on the opposite side. A concave (diverging) lens spreads parallel rays so that they appear to come from a virtual focal point on the same side as the object. Options A, C, and D are factually incorrect.

mcqs.question: The point on a thin lens through which a ray passes without being deviated is called:
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre (also called the centre of the lens) is the unique point where an incident ray emerges undeviated. The principal focus and focal point are locations where refracted rays converge or appear to diverge, while the principal axis is the line passing through the centre and the focal points.
